The script uses standard shell constructs and system utilities (`nmcli`, `busctl`, `systemctl`, `mkdir`, `printf`) in expected ways. While it accesses `/etc`, it does so only for its own configuration files, which is normal for system services.

The URL in the post-install message (`https://github.com/netmojo-systems/omdrop-plugin.git`) is presented as user guidance, not executed by the script, and is relevant to the application's functionality. This is consistent with standard packaging practices for plugins.

No evidence of supply-chain attack or malicious behavior is present.
